chunks.title: Conditions and Interventions

chunks.content:
Brief summary: The purpose of this study is to determine if intensive lowering of systolic blood pressure (SBP), using FDA approved medications (antihypertensive), reduces Alzheimer's Disease pathology (i.e., excessive brain amyloid and tau protein deposition) in older adults at high risk for memory decline or dementia.
Detailed description: The IPAT study is a 2-arm open-label randomized controlled trial to assess the effects of intensive pharmacological reduction of high blood pressure (SBP) on brain amyloid and tau protein deposition (Alzheimer's Disease pathology) in older adults who are at high risk for AD and related dementias, that is, those who have high blood pressure, family history of dementia, or subjective memory complaints. Furthermore, IPAT will examine effects of intensive blood pressure lowering on brain volume, perfusion, and neural network connectivity using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and cognitive performance.
chunks.title: Summary and Description
Eligibility

chunks.content:
type=primary | measure=Change From Baseline in Brain Fibrillar Beta-Amyloid Protein (Aβ) | time_frame=Baseline, 24 months | description=Brain Aβ will be measured by annual change of amyloid mean cortical standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) with positron emission tomography (PET).
type=secondary | measure=Change From Baseline in Brain Tau Deposition | time_frame=Baseline, 24 months | description=Brain Tau Deposition will be measured by tau temporal meta-ROI composite with positron emission tomography (PET).
type=secondary | measure=Change From Baseline in regional Cerebral Blood Flow (CBF) | time_frame=Baseline, 12 months, 24 months | description=Regional CBF will be measured by MRI using arterial spin labeling.
type=secondary | measure=Change From Baseline in global Cerebral Blood Flow (CBF) | time_frame=Baseline, 12 months, 24 months | description=Global CBF will be measured by PC-MRI and 2D color-coded duplex ultrasonography.
type=secondary | measure=Change From Baseline in Arterial Stiffness | time_frame=Baseline, 12months, 4 months | description=Central arterial stiffness (pulse wave velocity and carotid β-stiffness index) will be measured by artery applanation tonometry.
type=secondary | measure=Change From Baseline in Amplitude of Low Frequency Fluctuations of Blood-Oxygen-Level-Dependent Signal (BOLD ALFF) | time_frame=Baseline, 12 months, 24 months | description=BOLD ALFF will be measured by resting state functional MRI (rs-fMRI).
type=secondary | measure=Change From Baseline in White Matter Hyperintensity Volume | time_frame=Baseline, 12 months, 24 months | description=White matter hyperintensity volume will be measured by MRI using 3D T2 FLAIR sequence .
type=secondary | measure=Change From Baseline in Brain Neural Network Connectivity | time_frame=Baseline, 12 months, 24 months | description=Brain neural network connectivity will be measured by rs-fMRI.
type=secondary | measure=Change From Baseline in Neurocognitive Function | time_frame=Baseline, 12 months, 24 months | description=A composite z score will be obtained by conversion of individual test scores of the Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC) and the NIH Toolbox Cognition Battery to standardized z scores, then averaged to assess changes in global cognitive function. Domain-specific z scores will be used to assess specific domains of cognitive function (i.e., memory, executive function, language etc.).
